text.insert: A connection's visual path is never stored as a fixed drawing — it is computed from the current geometry of its two endpoint objects every time either side moves.

is the single object-to-object routing entry point: given the two endpoint objects and the connection's anchor/position/waypoint overrides, it returns a routed result — an SVG path, the true start and end anchor points, a label placement point, and the route's world-space vertex list. The router is style-agnostic: solid and dashed connectors share the same route, and there are no straight or smooth path algorithms.
Connections are a separate document collection with their own def — a

, and unlike object color edits, a picked connector color is not remembered for future connectors. Dashed rendering applies
Routing resolves in tiers. If stored

exist and form an orthogonal polyline, they win. Otherwise the router tries an exact straight route when facing anchors are already aligned, then builds a simple elbow path. Only when that simple elbow crosses an extra obstacle does it invoke the orthogonal A* pathfinder (
); if A* throws or yields no usable route, the already-computed simple elbow is the answer, so routing never fails outright.

Whichever tier produces the route, consecutive duplicate points are removed and the polyline becomes a rendered SVG path with rounded interior corners — the radius clamps to half the shorter adjacent segment so short segments get a sane smaller radius — and the first and last rendered points pull back by a fixed end-gap along their own tangent so the drawn stroke never touches the target border. The connection's
fields still carry the true, untouched anchor points for endpoint handles and label placement.

Routes are orthogonal by invariant. Stored waypoints are accepted only when every segment is orthogonal within 0.5 px; diagonal waypoint edits are ignored and auto-routing resumes. Nearly-straight A* output is flattened to an exact two-point route — the anchor may slide along the objects' edge-overlap span, trimmed by the end gap — so aligned objects get a straight line instead of a tiny dogleg.
Before any path is computed, the router decides which side of each endpoint object the connection attaches to.

prefers genuinely facing sides: if the objects' vertical spans overlap within an 8-px tolerance it picks right/left, if their horizontal spans overlap it picks bottom/top, and otherwise the dominant center separation wins, horizontal on ties. That pick is only the fallback — an explicit
side override wins when set, and an explicit relative
fraction of the object's bounds) overrides even the side, landing the endpoint at a specific point rather than a side midpoint.

handles the free-point preview while a connector is being dragged toward empty canvas: it anchors from the source object, picks the free endpoint side by dominant delta, and deliberately skips the A* obstacle pass while keeping the same rounded-corner and end-gap construction, so previews are cheap but look like committed routes.

Explicit waypoints are absolute world coordinates, so the routing layer does not keep them coherent when endpoints move — the reducer does, in the choke point wrapped around every document-changing action (

). The rule is asymmetric by design, per connection: when both endpoint owners translate by the same delta with no resize, waypoints translate rigidly, preserving trunk-and-branch fan shapes; when owners move asymmetrically or either resizes, waypoints are dropped so the connector re-routes rather than sweeping stale bends through space that no longer means anything. The same split applies to live-preview drag frames, so a fan of waypointed connectors visibly tracks a dragged section instead of snapping into place on drop. Duplicate and paste translate cloned waypoints by their offset at creation time.

exposes every orthogonal segment of a selected connector as a draggable bend handle; when a label lies on a segment, the handle shifts away from it so the pill stays reachable. Dragging is axis-constrained — horizontal segments move only vertically, vertical segments only horizontally — and a direct one-segment connector expands into a stub-run-stub polyline instead of disappearing. During the drag, same-orientation segment snaps and endpoint straightening use a zoom-scaled tolerance and simplify the preview the moment a snap lands.

simplifies the polyline: nearly-orthogonal segments normalize, tiny hooks and near-duplicates collapse, collinear triples merge. Waypoints are cleared only when the simplified route is straight; otherwise the interior corners persist as
. Reconnecting either endpoint clears existing waypoints, so old bends cannot survive an endpoint change.

decides where a dragged endpoint should snap. It iterates candidates in paint order and returns the first winner; for a candidate it requires the pointer inside the hover-expanded bounds, then tries the nearest cardinal anchor strictly within the screen-pixel snap radius, then the nearest outline point strictly within the world-pixel radius, then inside-shape resolution for eligible non-section shapes. No winner means
. Section interiors are deliberately free canvas — a drag across a section's body does not snap to it — but section anchors and outlines still participate in the higher tiers.

: four cardinal points offset outside the bounds and projected onto the object's real outline — ellipse curve, diamond, triangle, octagon, chevron — not its bounding box, with bbox fallback for every other kind. The same anchors feed the selected-object anchor dots and hit-testing, so attachment, affordance, and clicks can never disagree.
is a wiring mode, not a placeable object type. Pointer-down on a port starts a create gesture with a pinned

Completing or canceling a connection does not switch the tool back — the mode persists for wiring several connections in a row. props.covers: The connector behavioral model: connections are not objects, elbow/orthogonal routing with an A* fallback, anchor resolution, waypoint reconciliation, bend editing, the connection cascade, and the create/reconnect/quick-connect gestures plus Connector Mode.
